lessons.title: Networks: LAN, WAN and Their Benefits
lessons.notes_html:
A network is an interconnected system of ICT devices that share hardware and software resources, so users do not need a separate device or program for every computer. Users can exchange information and communicate with one another through the network.

LAN and WAN

A LAN (Local Area Network) is the interconnection of ICT devices in a small geographical area, such as a school, residence or laboratory. A WAN (Wide Area Network) is a global network of ICT devices that exists over a large-scale geographical area and connects different smaller networks, including LANs. For example, a banking system whose hundreds of branches in different cities are connected to share official data is a WAN.

Benefits of Using Networks

  • Computers in a network share hardware and software resources, so one printer or one program can serve many computers.
  • In a client-server network the server hosts, delivers and manages most of the resources and services requested by clients, such as print, web and file services.
  • Users can exchange information and communicate with one another through the network.

lessons.title: Network Devices
lessons.notes_html:
Special devices connect computers in a network and move messages between them. The four devices in this unit are the switch, the router, the NIC and the Wireless Access Point.

DeviceFunction
SwitchConnects computers by cable and sends a message directly to its destination computer.
RouterConnects two or more LANs and forwards a message by the best route to its destination.
NICThe card that lets a computer connect to a network to use hardware and software resources, including the Internet.
Wireless Access PointConnected to a wired network; lets devices transfer data wirelessly, extends wireless coverage and lets more users connect.

The Network Switch

A network switch is a device that allows computers in a network to connect with one another using wired communication. It receives a message from any device connected to the network and transmits that message directly to its destination computer, and it maintains a table (MAC table) for forwarding data. Unlike a hub, which sends data to all computers, the switch sends it only to the destination.

options: It sends the message to every computer on the network

mcqs.why: A switch receives a message from any connected device and transmits it directly to its destination computer, unlike a hub.

mcqs.why: The lesson's table says a router connects two or more LANs and forwards a message by the best route to its destination.

options: The card that lets a computer connect to a network
mcqs.why: NIC is the card that lets a computer connect to a network so it can use hardware and software resources, including the Internet.

mcqs.why: The lesson states that a Wireless Access Point is connected to a wired network and lets devices transfer data wirelessly.

mcqs.why: The switch maintains a table called the MAC table, which it uses for forwarding data to the right destination.

mcqs.why: Unlike a hub, which sends data to all computers, the switch sends it only to the destination computer.

mcqs.why: The lesson says a Wireless Access Point lets devices transfer data wirelessly, extends wireless coverage and lets more users connect.

mcqs.why: A network switch allows computers in a network to connect with one another using wired communication.

mcqs.why: The NIC lets a computer connect to a network to use hardware and software resources, including the Internet.

mcqs.why: The router forwards a message by the best route to its destination; the switch instead sends a message directly to its destination computer on its own network.

lessons.title: Wired and Wireless Networks
lessons.notes_html:
Data travels from one device to another through a transmission medium. Media are of two kinds: guided (wired) and unguided (wireless).

Guided (Wired) Media

  • Coaxial cable
  • Twisted pair cable
  • Fiber-optic cable - uses pulses of light through glass fiber, giving higher bandwidth and high-speed transmission over longer distances. In a communication environment with a high rate of distortion, fiber-optic cable is the most appropriate medium.

Unguided (Wireless) Media

  • Radio waves
  • Microwave
  • Infrared

Wired Network vs Wireless Network

A wired network uses guided media, that is cables, to transmit data. It gives high-speed, higher-bandwidth transmission over longer distances, but it needs physical cabling. A wireless network uses unguided media, that is radio waves, microwave and infrared, with no cables. It is easy to install and maintain, users can communicate while on the move, it provides faster transfer of information and the network is easy to expand.

The Data Communication Cycle

Data communication needs four parts: a sender, a message, a medium and a receiver. The sender sends the message along the medium to the receiver. A physical model of this cycle can be built with four labelled parts: a sender (for example a computer or phone), a medium (a string or cable joining them), a receiver (a second device) and a message card. To demonstrate it, write a short message on the card, pass it from the sender along the medium to the receiver, and have the receiver read it aloud.

lessons.title: Emerging Technologies
lessons.notes_html:
New technologies are changing how computers work and how people use them. The book introduces virtual reality, 3D holographic imaging, 5G, robotics, distributed applications and blockchain, and also names Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning among the new technologies.

Virtual Reality

Virtual reality creates a computer-generated simulation with objects and scenes that appear to be real.

3D Holographic Imaging

3D holographic imaging is a new technology that uses laser beams to create three-dimensional images called holograms. A 3D hologram displays objects and animations that seem to be real, it exists freely in space, and a person can walk around it and see it from all sides.

5G

5G is the 5th Generation cellular network technology developed to increase the speed of telecommunication networks.

Robotics

Robotics deals with the design, operation and application of robots to perform tasks traditionally done by human beings. According to the book, robots are widely used in automobile manufacturing, in packaging, in laboratory research and in cleaning homes.

Distributed Applications

A distributed application is computer software installed on servers in a network that runs on multiple computers at the same time to perform a single task. It is used when the workload is too much for a single server to handle. Examples are cellular networks, social networks, online banking and supermarket check-out systems.

Blockchain

Blockchain is a chain of blocks containing groups of information that cannot be changed or deleted. When information is filled in a block, it is closed and linked to other filled blocks to form a chain. Its purpose is the secure recording and sharing of digital information, and the blockchain database is used in banks and financial services for secure recording of transactions.

lessons.title: Microsoft Excel: Workbook and Worksheet
lessons.notes_html:
Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet software used for the analysis and storage of data in a tabular form. It is used to organize and manipulate data using formulas and functions.

Workbook and Worksheet

A workbook is a collection of one or more worksheets in a single file. A worksheet is a collection of cells organized in rows and columns that allows you to organize information as a table. In short, the workbook is the whole Excel file, while a worksheet is one table of cells inside it.

Cell

The basic unit of a worksheet into which you enter data is called a cell. A worksheet is a collection of cells organized in rows and columns.

The Formula Bar

The formula bar is the long bar marked with fx above the worksheet. It shows the formula or the contents of the active (selected) cell. In the book's result-sheet figures, the formula bar of cell H4 shows =AVERAGE(C4:F4) and that of cell I4 shows =IF(I4>=60, "Pass", "Fail"). Its purpose is to let the user view and edit the formula or data entered in the selected cell.

mcqs.why: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet software used for the analysis and storage of data in a tabular form, and to organize and manipulate data using formulas and functions.

lessons.title: Formulas and Functions
lessons.notes_html:
A formula is an expression that operates on values in a cell or a range of cells, and a formula always begins with an equality sign (=).

Useful Functions

FunctionUse
MAX( )Finds the highest value in a range, for example =MAX(G4:G8) finds the maximum marks obtained by a student in a class.
AVERAGE( )Finds the average of values, for example =AVERAGE(C4:F4).
IF( )Checks whether a condition is true or false and returns one value for a TRUE result and another for a FALSE result, for example =IF(I4>=60, "Pass", "Fail").
COUNT( )Counts the number of numeric entries present in a selection.
SUM( )Adds the numbers in a selection.

Uses of Microsoft Excel

  • Preparing a result sheet with obtained marks, averages, percentages and Pass/Fail remarks.
  • Arranging data in a specific order by sorting.
  • Showing data as a graph through charts such as column, bar, line and pie charts.

lessons.title: Charts in Excel
lessons.notes_html:
A chart is a graphical representation of data in a worksheet. Excel can draw column, bar, line and pie charts from worksheet data.

Steps to Create a Pie Chart

  • Step 1: Select the required cells that contain the data to be used in the chart, for example the name and percentage columns of the result sheet.
  • Step 2: Click the Chart button from the Insert tab.
  • Step 3: Click the required type of Chart, and for a pie chart choose the Pie chart type. Excel then draws the chart from the selected data.

lessons.title: The Information Processing Model
lessons.notes_html:
The computer's information processing model works in three stages. First some kind of input is obtained through input devices. Then the input is processed according to some given instructions. Then the output is generated through output devices, and the result may also be stored on storage or network devices.

Using this model, computers help us solve problems in a more effective and efficient way, performing billions of operations per second, so each operation is completed in a tiny fraction of a second. For larger and complex problems the input, process and output steps are repeated a number of times, producing intermediate results along the way.

lessons.title: Algorithms, Flowcharts and Pseudocode
lessons.notes_html:
Algorithm

An algorithm is the set of steps developed to solve a problem. After developing an algorithm, the next step is to write the program, and algorithms are converted to programs for execution on the computer.

Flowchart

A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm. It provides the flow of the steps of an algorithm in picture form.

Pseudocode

Pseudocode is written in plain English for humans. A program is intended for the machine, whereas pseudocode is intended for humans, so pseudocode is a way of writing down an algorithm in simple English steps before it is turned into a program.

Program (Code)

Code, the program, is what is directly input into the computer for execution. Pseudocode, flowcharts and algorithms are design representations, not machine input.

Variable

A variable refers to a memory location used to hold some data, and that data could be changed during the program execution. The value of a variable can be changed.

Constant

A constant is a value that does not change during the program execution.

Conditional Statements

Conditions are check points in a program which determine the flow of a program among possible branches based on variable values or events, so the program behaves according to the situation. A conditional statement checks whether a condition is true or false and then follows the matching branch.

lessons.title: Loops and Nested Loops
lessons.notes_html:
Loops (Repetition)

Repetition is a construct that allows the steps of an algorithm to be executed multiple times. Loops are used to repeat an action again and again, so the set of code is executed iteratively until the condition is met.

Nested Loops

A nested loop is a loop inside another loop: an outer loop (Loop1) containing an inner loop (Loop2). Nested loops always have as many loops as required.

Nested Loops and a Calendar

Nested loops are useful when an iterative task is to be done multiple times. A calendar is arranged by nesting in the same way as the book's clock example: the minute hand goes once around the clock every 60 minutes, making one hour and moving the hour hand. For a calendar, the outer loop runs for each month (or each week) and the inner loop runs for each day of that month, so the inner day loop completes fully for every single step of the outer month loop, filling the whole calendar day by day.

lessons.title: Scope and Limitations of a Problem
lessons.notes_html:
Scope

The scope of a problem defines the boundaries of what a solution must provide to meet the requirements. For example, for a simple calculator the scope is just four functionalities: Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication and Division.

Limitations

The limitation of a problem refers to the aspects that are beyond the study or implementation of the problem. For the same calculator, performing other operations such as percentage, square root, power and log is its limitation. In the email example in the book, a network fault is a limitation (you cannot resolve it at your end), while checking your own system's network settings is within the scope.

The book's activities give four pseudocodes to write. Each one is written in numbered lines, starting with Start and ending with End.

Line 1: Take input (number)

Line 4: ELSE:

Line 4: ELSE IF (number >= 10 AND number < 20) then:

lessons.title: Programming Constructs
lessons.notes_html:
The constructs of programming languages are sequence, condition and loop. Sequence means statements are executed in order. Condition means if and if-else statements. Loop means repeat, repeat-until and forever blocks.

Infinite Loop

A repeat until loop requires a matching condition, and as soon as the condition matches the loop terminates. If the condition never becomes TRUE, the loop never terminates and becomes an infinite loop.

The Floor Function

The Floor( ) function always rounds a number down to the nearest whole number below it.

lessons.notes_html:
The book's Python programs use input, if-else conditions and loops. Each program below is given exactly as in the solved exercise.

Leap Year

Take a 4-digit number as input for a year and check if the year is a leap year or not. Display the output as: "The year 1979 is not a leap year" or "The year 2020 is a leap year."
year = int(input("Enter a 4-digit year: "))
if (year % 400 == 0) or (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0):
print("The year", year, "is a leap year.")
else:
print("The year", year, "is not a leap year.")
For 1979: 1979 % 4 = 3, so it is not divisible by 4, and the program prints "The year 1979 is not a leap year". For 2020: 2020 % 4 = 0 and 2020 % 100 = 20 (not 0), so the program prints "The year 2020 is a leap year".

Square or Rectangle

Take length and width as input from the user for a quadrilateral and check if it is a square or rectangle.
length = float(input("Enter length: "))
width = float(input("Enter width: "))
if length == width:
print("It is a square.")
else:
print("It is a rectangle.")
A quadrilateral whose length and width are equal is a square; if they are different it is a rectangle.

Star Triangle

Print a triangle of stars, one star in row 1, two in row 2, up to five in row 5:
for i in range(1, 6):
print("* " * i)
This prints row 1 with one star, row 2 with two stars, row 3 with three stars, row 4 with four stars and row 5 with five stars, forming the triangle shown in the book.

Triangle of Squares

Display the squares of the numbers 1 to 10 in the form of a triangle: 1 / 4 9 / 16 25 36 / 49 64 81 100
num = 1
for row in range(1, 5):
line = ""
for col in range(row):
line = line + str(num * num) + " "
num = num + 1
print(line)
The outer loop runs for 4 rows; the inner loop prints 1 square in row 1, 2 squares in row 2, 3 squares in row 3 and 4 squares in row 4, using the numbers 1 to 10 squared in order: 1; 4 9; 16 25 36; 49 64 81 100.

Computer Ethics

Computer ethics means acceptable behavior for using digital technology. It is a set of rules to be followed for moral and social issues while using digital technology, particularly the Internet.

Copyright

Copyright is the branch of law which protects work from unauthorized use by other people. The person who expresses ideas in literary, artistic or any form is the natural owner of that form. Because no one else may legally copy, sell or use the work without the owner's consent, the creator alone can earn from it, for example by selling it or by allowing its use on payment, and others cannot take that income away by copying it freely.

Digital Piracy

Digital piracy means illegally copying digital content in any form without the consent of the owner. It is a crime because it breaks the copyright law that protects a creator's work from unauthorized use: the owner is deprived of the earnings from the work, while the pirate gains from something that is not theirs.

Cybercrime

Cybercrime refers to any crime committed by means of computer and Internet technology by having unlawful access to others' computers.

Why We Need Cybercrime Laws

We need cybercrime laws so that unlawful access, theft and misuse can be punished, victims have a proper place to report, and users, their privacy, their data and their money are protected by law when they use digital technology.

Reporting Cybercrime

To report a cybercrime in Pakistan, contact the NR3C, the National Response Centre for Cybercrime of the Federal Investigation Agency: www.nr3c.gov.pk. For queries about a complaint, the helpdesk email is helpdesk@nr3c.gov.pk.

Cyber Scout

A Cyber Scout is a person with the unique aim to promote awareness about cybercrime in society. He or she is trained to identify cybercrime activities and is equipped with adequate preventive knowledge to help fight this menace, understands the risks of virtual socializing, and works to promote cyber safety in his or her surroundings, creating cyber awareness among fellow students, teachers and parents.

How Cyber Scouts Help Prevent Cybercrime

  • Cybercrime awareness trainings
  • Cybercrime preventive measures
  • Sharing information with NR3C
  • Promoting careful and responsible use of cyberspace
  • Directing and helping individuals to report cybercrime
  • Patrolling cyberspace
  • Encouraging good moral use of technology

Malware

Malware is malicious software created to attack privacy and for spying, destruction and financial benefits. The book names virus, worm, adware and spyware among the types of malware.

MalwareWhat It Does
WormTransmits itself automatically over a network to infect other computers, without needing a host file or user action.
AdwareDisplays unwanted pop-up advertisements on the user's computer.
SpywareSecretly watches what the user does, records private information such as passwords and bank details, and passes it to criminals, which can lead to loss of privacy, theft of identity and loss of money.

Hackers

A hacker is a person who illegally breaks into others' computer systems for stealing or changing information, or to get credit card or bank details for financial benefits.

Why Computer Systems Should Be Protected

Computer systems should be protected from unauthorized access because unauthorized access lets criminals steal or change information and get credit card or bank details for financial benefits. Malware also attacks privacy, spies on users, destroys data and causes financial loss. Protection through passwords, careful use and antivirus software keeps private information, data and money safe.

lessons.title: The Business Plan
lessons.notes_html:
A business plan describes the company's goal, strategy and implementation for the growth of an organization. There are five components of a business plan.

ComponentMeaning
Customer needsThe market need - what the customers actually need.
Product designDesigning the product or service to meet that need.
CostingWorking out the cost of making the product and the price at which it will be sold.
OperationsHow the business will run day to day to produce and deliver the product.
MarketingHow the product will be promoted and sold to customers.

mcqs.q: What does a business plan describe?
options: The company's goal, strategy and implementation for the growth of an organization
mcqs.why: A business plan describes the company's goal, strategy and implementation for the growth of an organization, and it has five components.

mcqs.q: How many components does a business plan have?
mcqs.why: There are five components of a business plan: customer needs, product design, costing, operations and marketing.

mcqs.q: The "Customer needs" component of a business plan means what?
options: The market need — what the customers actually need
mcqs.why: Customer needs means the market need: what the customers actually need; product design then designs the product or service to meet that need.

mcqs.q: The "Product design" component means what?
options: Designing the product or service to meet the customer's need
Running the business day to day
mcqs.why: Product design is designing the product or service to meet the need identified in the customer needs component.

mcqs.q: The "Costing" component means what?
options: Working out the cost of making the product and the price at which it will be sold
mcqs.why: Costing is working out the cost of making the product and the price at which it will be sold.

mcqs.q: The "Operations" component means what?
options: How the business will run day to day to produce and deliver the product
How the product will be advertised
mcqs.why: Operations is how the business will run day to day to produce and deliver the product.

mcqs.q: The "Marketing" component of a business plan means what?
options: The cost of making the product
The day-to-day running of the business
How the product will be promoted and sold to customers
mcqs.why: Marketing, as a component of the business plan, is how the product will be promoted and sold to customers.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper first finds out what goods people in his area actually need. Which component is this?
mcqs.why: Finding the market need — what the customers actually need — is the customer needs component of the business plan.

mcqs.why: That is costing: working out the cost of making the product and the price at which it will be sold.

mcqs.why: Operations covers how the business will run day to day to produce and deliver the product.

lessons.title: Marketing and Its Four Elements
lessons.notes_html:
Marketing is the action or business of promoting and selling products or services, including market research and advertising.

The Four Elements of Marketing

ElementMeaning
ProductThe goods and services the business offers to the end user, which must be worth purchasing against competitors' products.
PriceAn important element decided keeping in mind the competitive price of the product.
PromotionThe packaging and position or place of the product in the marketplace where customers can be attracted, using marketing tools to promote sales.
PlaceThe location of the outlet and the mode of selling, whether by e-commerce, telephone or retail outlets.

Digital Marketing

Digital marketing is a tool used to promote brands and to connect with potential customers online, so it is often referred to as online marketing.

Social Media Marketing

Social media marketing uses digital platforms such as Facebook, YouTube and Twitter to promote products or services, so it is a type of digital marketing.

Advantages of Digital Marketing

  • It has removed all sorts of geographical barriers, so products can be promoted worldwide.
  • Reduction in costs through automation and use of electronic media, with extremely low risk.
  • Faster response to both marketers and the end users, increased exposure of products or services, and winning customer loyalty.

Disadvantages of Digital Marketing

  • It depends on technology, so it fails where technology or connectivity is missing.
  • Security and privacy issues for users and businesses.
  • Maintenance cost is more due to a constantly evolving environment, along with higher transparency of pricing, increased price competition and worldwide competition through globalization.

options: The action or business of promoting and selling products or services, including market research and advertising
mcqs.why: Marketing is the action or business of promoting and selling products or services, including market research and advertising.

mcqs.why: The four elements of marketing are Product, Price, Promotion and Place.

mcqs.why: Product is the goods and services the business offers to the end user, which must be worth purchasing against competitors' products.

options: The competitive price of the product

options: The packaging and position or place of the product in the marketplace where customers can be attracted, using marketing tools to promote sales

lessons.title: Transactions and Payments
lessons.notes_html:
Transaction

A transaction is an agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services or financial assets in return for money. It is the act of conducting or carrying out business.

Payment

Payment is the transfer of money against the purchase of goods or services. It is the act of paying within that business, and it can be made by credit cards, debit cards, bank transfer or Easypaisa.

In short, the transaction is the whole deal between buyer and seller, while the payment is the money part of it.

mcqs.q: What is a transaction?
options: An agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services or financial assets in return for money
mcqs.why: A transaction is an agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services or financial assets in return for money; it is the act of conducting or carrying out business.

mcqs.why: The lesson defines a transaction as the act of conducting or carrying out business between a buyer and a seller.

options: The whole deal between buyer and seller
The transfer of money against the purchase of goods or services
mcqs.why: Payment is the transfer of money against the purchase of goods or services — the act of paying within that business.

mcqs.why: Payment can be made by credit cards, debit cards, bank transfer or Easypaisa, as the lesson lists.

mcqs.why: Easypaisa is one of the payment methods named in the lesson, along with credit cards, debit cards and bank transfer.

mcqs.why: The exchange in a transaction is in return for money, and the payment is the transfer of that money against the purchase.

mcqs.why: Payment is the act of paying within the business — the money part — while the transaction is the whole deal between buyer and seller.

lessons.title: Quality and Quality Assurance
lessons.notes_html:
Quality

Quality is all about meeting the needs and expectations of customers with respect to functionality, design, reliability, durability and price of the product.

Assurance

Assurance is a positive declaration on a product or service which gives confidence to the user.

Quality Assurance

Quality Assurance is a procedure to ensure the quality of a product or service. It focuses on improving the development process and making it efficient and effective as per the quality standards defined for products, through steps such as taking measures, identifying the problem area, identifying indicators, preparing criteria, comparing results and analysing assessment. Verification is checking against the defined criteria and standards, which is the assurance activity in that process.

Quality Assurance is important because it helps a company design and create a product which meets the expectations of customers and produces a high quality product that builds up the trust and loyalty of the customers.

options: Only the price of a product
Meeting the needs and expectations of customers with respect to functionality, design, reliability, durability and price of the product
mcqs.why: Quality is all about meeting the needs and expectations of customers with respect to functionality, design, reliability, durability and price of the product.

mcqs.why: Quality concerns functionality, design, reliability, durability and price of the product, judged against the needs and expectations of customers.

mcqs.why: Checking against the defined criteria and standards — verification — is the assurance activity in the Quality Assurance process.

mcqs.why: A high quality product builds up the trust and loyalty of the customers, which is why Quality Assurance is important.

lessons.title: Marketing Strategy in Practice: PIA
lessons.notes_html:
Pakistan Airline (PIA) plans to offer incentives to their valuable customers. This activity chalks out a marketing strategy to promote the PIA offer using digital platforms and social media marketing, using the book's digital marketing tools.

  • Product and value proposition: present the incentive as an innovation that makes flying PIA more attractive, for example bonus miles, discounted tickets for frequent flyers, extra baggage allowance and priority check-in for valuable customers.
  • Digital platforms: promote the offer worldwide through digital platforms such as Facebook, YouTube and Twitter, plus PIA's website and mobile app, since a digital platform is an electronic tool to promote products or services worldwide.
  • Promotion: create awareness to increase sales with short videos of the offer, "Buy 1 Get 1 free"-style deals on selected routes, and social media marketing posts that draw the attention of end users and encourage immediate booking.
  • Place and payment: let customers book and pay online through the website and app using credit cards, debit cards, bank transfer or Easypaisa, so the whole transaction from offer to ticket is digital.
  • Search Engine Optimization: improve PIA's website visibility so people searching for flights and offers in Google, Bing and other search engines find the incentive offer first.

mcqs.why: Pakistan Airline (PIA) plans to offer incentives to their valuable customers, and the activity chalks out a marketing strategy to promote the offer.

mcqs.why: Because customers book and pay online through the website and app, the whole transaction from offer to ticket is digital.
